title: Optimization Attribution Waterfall
description: A waterfall chart connecting a baseline execution time to a final time through four individually measured optimization steps, switchable between microseconds and percentage of baseline.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Performance Engineering
Benchmarking

educational.topic: Attributing a total speedup to individual optimizations
learningObjectives: Assess each optimization's contribution to a total speedup
Justify keeping or dropping a change from its measured share
Recognize that attribution depends on the order changes were applied
prerequisites: Familiarity with the four named optimizations

controls.label: Show as percentage of baseline
controls.purpose: Relative view that rescales every bar and label

controls.label: Bar
controls.purpose: Show the change, its share of the speedup, and what it was

controls.label: Bar
controls.purpose: Tooltip with the exact delta and share

equations: final = 710 us, total saved = 140 us, speedup = 1.20x
assumptions: Values are illustrative, stated in the title and in a documentation admonition
Each step was measured with all earlier steps already applied
Every measurement came from the same harness on the same hardware
limitations: Attribution is order-dependent; a different application order gives different per-step numbers
Shows a single run per step, with no variance or confidence interval

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal allocation of a known total, followed by a decision under a stated requirement
keyQuestions: Which change earned the most, and which one cost the most to write?
What would this chart look like if the steps were applied in a different order?
commonMisconceptions: That a before/after pair tells you which change worked
That the cleverest-sounding optimization is the most valuable
That per-step contributions are independent of ordering
assessmentOpportunities: Recommend keeping or dropping a 3% step and name the missing information
Decide which subset of changes meets a stated timing requirement
